item.title: Iran’s War Strategy: Don’t Calibrate—Escalate
item.description: Threatened by regime change and determined to deter future attacks, Iran is opting for unbridled escalation in its war against the United States and Israel.

item.title: Abracadabra
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch analyzes the impact of the war on Iran on energy supply chains, foreign investment, and global manufacturing.

item.title: Government as a Demand Creator for the Quantum Industry
item.description: To secure quantum leadership, the federal government should act as a credible demand creator—not just a funder of research and development and an ecosystem enabler. A federal funding ladder de-risks private investment and carries quantum technologies across the valley of death.

item.title: Investing in National Assets for Quantum Commercialization
item.description: Decades of public investment, world class research institutions, and the emergence of multiple high-performing regional innovation ecosystems have positioned the United States as a leader in quantum. Yet this position is neither assured nor self-sustaining.

item.title: Iran War Cost Estimate Update: $11.3 Billion at Day 6, $16.5 Billion at Day 12
item.description: This update uses the DOD-reported $11.3 billion war cost to calculate the impact on munition inventories. It also estimates the cost of combat losses and damage to bases ($1.7 billion) and the total cost over 12 days of Epic Fury ($16.5 billion).

item.title: Trump May Seize Iran’s Nuclear Stockpile: Why Airstrikes Alone Aren’t Enough
item.description: Air strikes are not sufficient to neutralize Iran’s nuclear threat. Post Operation Epic Fury, President Trump is weighing options to secure the remaining stockpile, with the Department of Defense moving assets into the region to enable a potential seizure operation.

item.title: Nepal’s Election Marks a Generational Break—and a New Strategic Moment in the Himalayas
item.description: Nepal’s election signals more than a political upset. Balendra “Balen” Shah’s youth-driven victory marks a generational break in Kathmandu and could reshape how India, China, and the United States navigate a new strategic moment in the Himalayas.
